external_entities.name: developers
external_entities.description: People who push branches and can log in to the build runner to initiate rebuilds.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server

external_entities.name: public package registry
external_entities.description: The public package registry on the internet used during dependency resolution.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Dependency resolution reaches out to the public package registry on the internet

processes.name: build runner
processes.description: Picks up merges, fetches source, resolves the dependency lockfile, produces container images, pushes images, calls the deploy controller, and permits developers to initiate manual rebuilds.
processes.source_excerpt: The build runner picks the merge up, fetches the source, resolves the dependency lockfile and produces a container image.

processes.name: deploy controller
processes.description: Maintains the current image release record and responds to release queries from store servers.
processes.source_excerpt: The deploy controller runs on the corporate network and holds one record: which image sha the estate should be on.
processes.notes: The runner uses a shared build token to call it. The authentication presented by store servers is undocumented.

processes.name: store server
processes.description: A small server in each of about 1,200 stores that runs the till software container, polls the deploy controller, pulls images, and restarts the container when the release changes.
processes.source_excerpt: Every store server asks the deploy controller once a minute what the current release is
processes.notes: There are about 1,200 store servers. Nobody has written down what a store server presents to the registry or controller.

processes.name: till software
processes.description: Software running as a container on each store server.
processes.source_excerpt: running the till software as a container

data_stores.name: self-hosted git server
data_stores.description: Git server on the corporate network receiving developer branches and merges to main.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server, which sits on the corporate network.

data_stores.name: image registry
data_stores.description: Registry in the build environment storing finished container images tagged with commit SHAs and allowing store servers to pull them.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It pushes the finished image to our image registry, which is also in the build environment.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has documented whether the image registry encrypts what it stores.

data_flows.name: push branches
data_flows.description: Developers push branches to the self-hosted git server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server

data_flows.name: fetch source
data_flows.description: The build runner picks up a merge and fetches source from the self-hosted git server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The build runner picks the merge up, fetches the source
data_flows.notes: A merge to main starts a build.

data_flows.name: push image
data_flows.description: The build runner pushes the finished container image to the image registry.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It pushes the finished image to our image registry
data_flows.notes: Images are tagged with the commit SHA.
data_flows.data_description: finished container image tagged with the commit SHA

data_flows.name: set release
data_flows.description: The build runner calls the deploy controller and asks it to make an image the current release.
data_flows.source_excerpt: When the image is pushed the runner calls the deploy controller and asks it to make that image the current release.
data_flows.notes: The runner uses a shared build token that is the same for every pipeline and has not been rotated since the pipeline was set up.

data_flows.name: query release
data_flows.description: Each store server asks the deploy controller what the current release is.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every store server asks the deploy controller once a minute what the current release is
data_flows.notes: Nobody has written down what a store server presents to the controller.
data_flows.data_description: current release query and image SHA response

data_flows.name: pull image
data_flows.description: A store server pulls the current container image from the image registry when its running image differs from the current release.
data_flows.source_excerpt: if it differs from what it is running it pulls that image from the registry
data_flows.notes: The image registry allows the pull; nobody has written down what a store server presents to it.

data_flows.name: resolve dependencies
data_flows.description: The build runner reaches out to the public package registry to resolve dependencies.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Dependency resolution reaches out to the public package registry on the internet
data_flows.notes: The runner does not verify signatures on what it downloads.
data_flows.data_description: dependency packages and lockfile resolution requests

data_flows.name: start rebuild
data_flows.description: A developer logs in to the build runner and manually initiates a rebuild of main.
data_flows.source_excerpt: any developer can log in to the build runner and kick off a rebuild of `main` by hand
data_flows.notes: This path does not require a merge and is not reviewed.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network zone containing the self-hosted git server and deploy controller.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: which sits on the corporate network

trust_boundaries.name: build environment
trust_boundaries.description: A build environment separate from the corporate network containing the build runner and image registry.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The runner lives in its own build environment, separate from the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: store estate
trust_boundaries.description: The estate of store servers in approximately 1,200 stores.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The image registry is reachable from the store estate over the WAN.

trust_boundaries.name: internet
trust_boundaries.description: The public internet zone containing the public package registry.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the public package registry on the internet

assumptions.assumption: The build runner presents a non-web interface because it is described as a build runner that performs batch builds.
assumptions.basis: The text describes the build runner as picking up merges, fetching source, resolving dependencies, and producing images, with no web application interface.

assumptions.assumption: The store server presents a non-web interface because it is described as polling controllers and pulling images rather than presenting a web application.
assumptions.basis: The text describes periodic polling and image pulls by each store server.

assumptions.assumption: The self-hosted git server stores confidential data because it stores source code and branches for the build pipeline.
assumptions.basis: The text says developers push branches and source is fetched from the self-hosted git server; source code is commercially sensitive system data.
